title: Input context flags, predicate-gated action views and native UI navigation
status: Reviewed static instruction and data flow for the October executable. No live input-ownership contract or callable Wasm API is established by this map.

controls_object.lifetime: The getter has guarded lazy initialization. A mapped static address alone does not establish initialized state or a safe arbitrary-thread read.
controls_object.script_query: nl_player_controls_enabled returns (raw_flags & 0xc00) == 0xc00 through callback 0x1a40cf0 and query 0x29d70a0.
controls_object.script_writer: nl_player_enable_controls passes its Boolean to 0x29d70e0 with the third argument true, selecting raw bit 10. The other selector branch writes bit 11.
controls_object.native_writer: State application 0x25477c0 sets both raw bits when its source configuration bit 6 is set. Generic flag mutator 0x29d7220 can OR or clear an arbitrary supplied mask. The reviewed direct setter callers are not an exhaustive writer census.

derived_context.sequence: Save raw and derived previous values, then clear and recompute the derived word from raw flags before constructing input views.
derived_context.raw_query_is_insufficient: Raw flags 0xc00 satisfy the Lua controls-enabled query but produce a zero derived word in the reducer. Raw control enablement is not input-context eligibility.
derived_context.bit_1_dependency: The reducer may set derived bit 1 only after selecting a context with derived bit 0, passing its higher-priority branches, and observing raw bit 10. Raw bit 11 is not read by this reducer.
derived_context.rising_transition: 0x2541f70 compares derived bit 1 before and after the update and invokes 0x29c88e0 on a false-to-true transition. The helper's complete reset semantics are not established here.
derived_context.names: Derived bit meanings are identified numerically. Complete engine context names and menu/text-capture relationships have not been established.

action_views.guards: Both readers require a backend, matching generation (or the all-ones wildcard), an accepting optional predicate, and a usable input source. A false predicate returns no action value. An absent predicate bypasses only that predicate check.
action_views.player_consumer: heron::player_input::update_analog_inputs::variableSystem reaches worker 0x22c96f0, which reads the action view at input-environment offset 0x138 through these readers. Population 0x1a93b40 copies this view from controls-object offset 0x148 through accessor 0x29d6d30 and copy helper 0x1a94470, preserving its derived-bit-1 predicate.

environment_copy.selection: The accessor selects controls-object offset 0x148 only while the connection pointer at offset 0 is nonzero. Otherwise it returns the static empty fallback; stale embedded view data is not evidence of a connected player view.
environment_copy.predicate_lifetime: The copy helper clones the source predicate through vtable slot 0 before installing its wrapper. Bit-1 clone and move functions copy the vtable and the borrowed controls-object pointer. They do not clone the controls object.
environment_copy.assignment: Context update builds a temporary block and assigns it into controls-object offset 0x10 using 0x29d7fb0. Its third view, block offset 0x138, therefore occupies controls-object offset 0x148. That view carries the derived-bit-1 predicate.
environment_copy.limits: The pointer chain is statically established for this population path. Population frequency, later environment mutation and an exhaustive census of alternate producers are not established; a controls-object observation is not an atomic snapshot of every ECS environment.

ui_navigation.eligibility: The context name must match a currently applied state and pass stack activity. A missing input object, context byte +0x5e and countdown +0x64 can additionally skip polling.
ui_navigation.limits: An eligible context is positive evidence for that UI navigation path. Absence of polling is not proof of gameplay ownership; mouse, text entry and other UI consumers are outside this trace. Byte +0x5e is reset within the worker and must not be treated as a durable global menu flag.

integration_boundaries: Do not authorize guest suppression from foreground focus, the Lua raw-controls query, or absence of UI navigation polling.
Sample on a reviewed engine phase and copy bounded observations; do not invoke predicate vtables or singleton initialization from a Wasm worker.
Establish input-view identity, generation and replacement before retaining any engine-derived observation.
Keep native cancel and system shortcuts available. Unknown, stale, loading and non-gameplay context must not renew a future suppression lease.
Menu, dialog, text entry, key capture and reload behavior need independent evidence before any derived bit is named exclusive gameplay ownership.

observation.edge: After successful return; a pending or unwound update invalidates the cache.
observation.scope: Optional copied raw/derived flags, connection state, reviewed third-view predicate identity, backend generation match, source availability and callback thread ID. The sampler does not invoke engine methods or write controls data; the hook forwards the original update unchanged. No input suppression or Wasm ownership flag.
observation.guards: Disconnected controls skip embedded view inspection. Backend and generation eligibility precede predicate dereferences; an accepting reviewed predicate precedes fallback-source dereferences. source_checked distinguishes skipped source evaluation from a missing source. Observed identity or state churn clears the sample.
observation.limits: Exact reviewed build and entry fingerprint required; the hotfix has a separate related map. Snapshots expire after 100 ms and are not permission to mutate input. At most 64 semantic changes are logged, no more often than every 250 ms; thread migration alone does not spend the budget. This is not complete transition capture. Game menu, text-entry, loading and reload behavior remain unconfirmed.

menu_mode.identity: The current executable names this variable-update system menuModeSystem and its query UINavigationContextSimple.
menu_mode.eligibility: The worker requires a player-context getter and GameReadiness byte +1. The helper enumerates navigation contexts, matches their names against applied UI stack states and requires stack activity. A match sets menu-present and copies context byte +0x5c; a later match can overwrite the second output.
menu_mode.transitions: The worker compares menu-present with controls raw bit 5. A mismatch queues request type 3 to leave or type 5/6 to enter, selected by the helper second output. Helpers 0x1b71180, 0x1b711f0 and 0x1b71260 append through 0x1b722f0 to a 0x48-stride request vector. This is deferred request production, not an immediate controls write.
menu_mode.application: State configuration application 0x25477c0 maps configuration bits 1, 2, 3 and 10 to controls raw bits 4, 7, 5 and 15 respectively. Transition processing also writes raw bit 7 independently. Exact request-type to configuration selection remains unresolved.
menu_mode.limits: Positive menu requests are a concrete observation lead. Absence of a match is not exclusive gameplay permission. Request application latency, context byte +0x5c semantics, text entry and coverage of other UI consumers remain unverified.

machine_abi.worker: void(query temporary address in RCX, UIStateStacks address in RDX, TransitionRequest Ptr-wrapper address in R8, GameReadiness Ptr-wrapper address in R9). The query is a caller-owned 32-byte temporary, not an ECS world pointer.
machine_abi.helper: void(query address in RCX, UIStateStacks address in RDX, uint8_t* matched_active_context in R8, uint8_t* last_match_flag_5c in R9). Return register contents are not a Boolean result.
machine_abi.output_lifetime: The reviewed worker zero-initializes two stack bytes before calling the helper. The helper does not initialize outputs; it sets the first byte to one on any match and overwrites the second with the raw +0x5c byte for each match. Copy only on normal helper return before returning to this caller; do not retain addresses.
machine_abi.raw_bit_correlation: Worker latches raw bit5 before helper execution. Reading raw controls after the helper is a separate observation, not that latched value or proof of exact transition choice.
machine_abi.scope: Machine-level ABI for this reviewed call path only. The optional native observer copies completed outputs from this call path; live coverage remains unverified. No exclusive gameplay or text-ownership permission follows from negative or absent menu observations.

observation.activation: The input-context.enabled marker opts into both independent native observers on the reviewed October update and hotfix profiles; hotfix addresses are recorded in the separate related map. The helper observer checks its instruction fingerprint and caller return address before copying outputs.
observation.lifetime: The original helper receives all four arguments unchanged. Only normally returned, initially zeroed output bytes are copied; no engine pointer is retained. In-flight, overlapping, unwound or older-than-100ms observations are unknown.
observation.logging: At most 64 semantic changes, sampled no faster than every 250ms. Status and observed fields trigger records; thread migration alone does not spend the budget. Records include the callback thread ID. Separate controls and menu records do not form a coherent engine-frame snapshot.
observation.evidence: Native tests cover borrowing, argument forwarding, rejected contracts, expiration, overlap and exception propagation. Actual menu coverage and text-entry ownership require gameplay evidence. This observer does not grant or change input suppression.

text_input_notification.identity: The PageContent listener slot references the imported Cohtml IViewListener::OnTextInputTypeChanged default callback. No game-defined override storing a capture flag is established by this trace.
text_input_notification.limits: This identifies a possible observation boundary only. ControlType values, actual notification delivery, active-page identity and destruction/replacement must be established before exposing text capture or granting suppression.
